meta.title: JoVee — everything you and your band need
meta.desc: Amps, pedals, TONE3000, stems, tab, drums, looper and tuner in one app for guitar, bass and vocals. macOS, Windows and Linux.
hero.h1: Everything you and your band need.
hero.free: The full JoVee Rig is free until December 31, 2026.
hero.alt: JoVee Rig with one chain per instrument
dl.sub: Every installer of the latest JoVee Rig version.
fam.sub: Each app does one thing. Rig is available now; the others are coming soon.
fam.studio: Record, edit, mix and finish songs across multiple tracks, with Rig inside.
fam.tone: Recreates a recording's tone by measuring it and sets it up on Rig.
fam.lut: Guides your guitar setup step by step, measuring each string by its sound.
fam.live: Play live over the internet with other musicians, each on their own rig and with their own monitor mix.
fam.school: An electric guitar course from zero to advanced in rock, blues and metal, that listens to you play to measure your progress.
cta.h2: Download JoVee Rig and plug in your guitar.
portal.sub: From the first chord to rehearsal, one app for every moment of playing.
step.school.h: Start from zero and see how far you have come.
step.rig.h: Amps, cabs and pedals on your computer.
step.tone.h: The recording's tone, on your rig.
step.studio.h: Record the whole song at home.
step.live.h: Rehearse with your band, each at home.
ap.jam.lede: Add a song, split the band into tracks and play along with the tab and the lyrics scrolling.
ap.jam.how.h2: Add the song and play with its band.
ap.jam.s1.p: Search for it inside the app or bring it from your computer.
ap.jam.s2.p: Drums, bass, vocals, guitar, piano and the rest, each on its own track.
ap.jam.s3.p: Level, pan, mute and solo per track: take the guitar out and play in its place.
ap.jam.s4.p: Jam listens to you and marks each note on time, late, wrong or missed.
ap.jam.f.h2: Everything you need to play a whole song.
ap.jam.f1.p: Imported, or generated from the separated guitar, and refretted for your tuning.
ap.jam.f2.p: Lyrics with chords, the line being sung lit up.
ap.jam.f3.p: Your Rig tone changes by itself at the points of the song you mark.
ap.jam.f4.p: A count-in before you come in and each section’s name spoken on time.
ap.jam.f5.p: Fix notes, chords and lyric lines by hand.
ap.jam.f6.p: Filter your songs by artist and by the tracks already split.
ap.tone.lede: Pick a song: Tone measures the guitar tone on the recording and builds it in your Rig.
ap.tone.how.h2: From the record to your rig, measuring note by note.
ap.tone.s1.p: Search for it and bring in the recording’s audio.
ap.tone.s2.p: Tone looks up the gear used on the record, with a source for each piece.
ap.tone.s3.p: Each guitar note on the record is compared with the same note played on your guitar.
ap.tone.s4.p: The result becomes a ready preset in JoVee Rig.
ap.tone.f.h2: What Tone uses to reach the record’s tone.
ap.tone.f1.p: Splits the guitar from the song to find where it plays and which note it is.
ap.tone.f2.p: Measures chords as well as single notes, low string included.
ap.tone.f3.p: Half a step down, a whole step down and drop D down to B.
ap.tone.f4.p: Record each note of your guitar once; Tone compares against it.
ap.tone.f5.p: Pick which guitar of the song to measure.
ap.tone.f6.p: Limit the measurement to the minutes you choose.
ap.lut.lede: It says what to play, listens to your guitar and tells you which screw to turn, and which way.
ap.lut.how.h2: A setup step by step, listening to each string.
ap.lut.s1.p: The app says which string or note to play.
ap.lut.s2.p: It measures by sound what is out of place.
ap.lut.s3.p: Plain words plus a drawing of the part, the tool and the turn.
ap.lut.s4.p: It listens again until it is right, and shows the before and after.
ap.lut.f.h2: A full setup, in the right order.
ap.lut.f1.p: Fresh strings tuned to pitch before anything else.
ap.lut.f2.p: Measured with a ruler or feeler gauge, with a drawing of where to measure.
ap.lut.f3.p: How much to raise or lower each bridge saddle.
ap.lut.f4.p: Which side and how far to turn each pickup screw.
ap.lut.f5.p: Where to move each saddle so fret 12 matches the open string.
ap.lut.f6.p: At the end, a PDF with what each stage found and how it was left.
ap.studio.lede: Record, edit, mix and finish songs on many tracks, with JoVee Rig on every track.
ap.studio.how.h2: From the first take to the finished song.
ap.studio.s1.p: Arm many tracks and record from any input, hearing yourself through the Rig.
ap.studio.s2.p: Cut, move, trim and fade clips; the original file is never changed.
ap.studio.s3.p: Faders, pan, sends, buses and groups, with automation on any control.
ap.studio.s4.p: The mix and each track apart, as WAV, FLAC or MP3.
ap.studio.f.h2: A complete studio, with your rig inside.
ap.studio.g1.i1: Every track has its own chain with the Rig's blocks (native, IR, NAM, TONE3000, VST3), or copies a chain from the open Rig
ap.studio.g1.i2: Audio tracks (WAV, MP3, FLAC) and MIDI tracks
ap.studio.g1.i3: Arm, mute, solo, fader and pan on every track
ap.studio.g1.i4: Monitor the chain live without arming, and freeze a track to save CPU
ap.studio.g1.i5: Every take keeps the clean DI, so you can re-amp it later through a new chain
ap.studio.g1.i6: Punch in on the A–B loop, record in a loop keeping each pass as a take, and build the track from the best parts of each take
ap.studio.g1.i7: A count-in of 1 to 4 bars before recording, and a click with an accent on the first beat
ap.studio.g1.i8: Stems separated in JoVee Stem come in as tracks
ap.studio.g2.i1: Move, trim, split, copy, paste, duplicate and delete
ap.studio.g2.i2: Fade, gain and an automatic crossfade where two clips overlap
ap.studio.g2.i3: Stretch in time without changing the pitch, and the clip follows the song's tempo
ap.studio.g2.i4: Snap to the grid, from whole notes to sixteenth notes
ap.studio.g2.i5: The original file is never changed
ap.studio.g3.i1: Tempo typed in or tapped, and tempo and time signature changes at any point
ap.studio.g3.i2: Sections (Intro, Verse, Chorus): dragging a section moves everything inside it, and you can duplicate or delete it
ap.studio.g3.i4: Import Guitar Pro (.gp, .gpx, .gp5, .gp4, .gp3, .gtp): tempo, sections, chords and the tab on screen
ap.studio.g3.i5: The same markers as JoVee Jam: name, spoken count-in, tone change per track, and MIDI and pedalboard commands
ap.studio.g4.i2: Velocity, controllers (modulation, volume, pan, expression, sustain) and quantize
ap.studio.g4.i3: Instruments: the JoVee drum kit or an LV2/VST3 plugin
ap.studio.g5.i1: Mixer with a live meter on every channel
ap.studio.g5.i2: Master with its own chain (EQ, compressor, limiter…)
ap.studio.g5.i3: Aux buses with sends before or after the fader
ap.studio.g5.i4: Folder tracks, VCA faders and groups that move together
ap.studio.g5.i5: Automation of volume, pan and any knob, in Read, Write, Touch and Latch modes
ap.studio.g5.i7: An output of its own for each track
ap.studio.g5.i8: Render a track in place or to a new track
ap.studio.g5.i9: A color for each track, and drag to reorder
ap.studio.g6.i1: New song, open, recents, save as (takes the audio along) and autosave
ap.studio.g6.i2: Export the mix as WAV, FLAC or MP3, normalized to -1 dBTP or -14 LUFS, in 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float, with dither
ap.studio.g6.i3: Export each track as a separate WAV, aligned from the start
ap.studio.g7.i2: Mackie Control surface: transport and the first 8 channels
ap.studio.g7.i3: MIDI learn: any controller drives transport, faders, mute, solo, sends and knobs, with presets shared across the JoVee apps
ap.studio.g7.i4: MCP and gRPC: everything the screen does can be done from outside (AI, a remote app)
ap.live.lede: Play live with other musicians over the internet: your rig’s sound goes straight to them and theirs comes back to your headphones.
ap.live.how.h2: Band rehearsal with each one at home.
ap.live.s1.p: Each musician plays through their own Rig.
ap.live.s2.p: Two to six musicians, connected straight to each other, no server in between.
ap.live.s3.p: Set each musician’s level in your own headphones.
ap.live.s4.p: In the same city, the estimated delay is 8 to 15 ms over a wired connection.
ap.live.f.h2: Built for the timing of the music.
ap.live.f1.p: Your rig’s processed sound is sent, so nobody needs your plugins.
ap.live.f2.p: About 0.5 Mbps of upload each, in a five-piece band.
ap.live.f3.p: The connection runs apart from your rig’s audio and never gets in its way.
ap.live.f4.p: Your monitor mix is yours; the others’ mixes don’t change.
ap.live.f5.p: No virtual cables and no second app.
ap.live.f6.p: Play along with a teacher or another student.
ap.school.lede: Say what you want to play, pick the method, and the app listens to you to decide when you move on.
ap.school.how.h2: From the first chord to the band, one step at a time.
ap.school.s1.p: Play with friends, solo, metal, write and record, or go far: the course shows what you need.
ap.school.s2.p: Follow the JoVee School path or the order of recognised music schools.
ap.school.s3.p: Each lesson has tab, notation, a diagram, audio and the fingering.
ap.school.s4.p: Right notes, timing and consistency decide when you pass, with a retest the next day.
ap.school.f.h2: What the course teaches and measures.
ap.school.f1.p: Eight phases, from the first note to advanced.
ap.school.f2.p: At the end of phase 4 you can play in a band; the rest is specialisation.
ap.school.f3.p: Power chords come before open chords, so you play riffs early.
ap.school.f4.p: From the first phase; theory comes once you already play the sound.
ap.school.f5.p: Part of the path, for rock and metal.
ap.school.f6.p: Say how much time you have per day and the schedule follows.
fam.rig: Build each instrument's rig with amps, cabs and pedals, in any order you want.
fam.jam: Add a song and play along with the band, the tab and the lyrics.
ap.rig.f.h2: Each instrument with its own rig, and everything to practise and play live around it.
ap.rig.g1.i1: One chain per instrument (electric, acoustic, bass, voice, keys or drums), and the block list shows only that instrument's blocks
ap.rig.g1.i2: Several instruments on the same interface at once, each one apart from the others
ap.rig.g1.i3: Each chain is drawn as a graph: "+" on any wire adds a block right there, and you drag blocks to reorder them
ap.rig.g1.i4: Split the signal into as many paths as you want, even inside another path: Split → Mix sums them with level, pan and polarity per path, Split → Y sends each path to its own outputs
ap.rig.g1.i5: Insert: send the signal out to a hardware pedal and bring it back in the middle of the chain
ap.rig.g1.i6: An output or an input in the middle of the chain, to tap the signal after any block or bring in a second source
ap.rig.g1.i7: One chain plays on several outputs, and two interfaces at different sample rates work in the same project
ap.rig.g1.i8: Measure the chain's latency from input to output, stage by stage
ap.rig.g2.i1: Built-in amps, preamps and cabs, plus overdrive, distortion, fuzz, compressor, gate, EQ, wah and pitch shifter
ap.rig.g2.i2: 14 delays (tape, BBD, ping-pong, granular, pitch…) and 13 reverbs (spring, plate, hall, shimmer…)
ap.rig.g2.i3: 16 modulations: chorus, flanger, phaser, tremolo, vibrato, rotary and ring modulator
ap.rig.g2.i4: Your own .nam captures and IRs, loaded from any folder
ap.rig.g2.i5: LV2 and VST3 plugins in the same chain; a VST3 opens its own window
ap.rig.g2.i6: Delays and modulations follow the project tempo by note value: 1/4, dotted 1/8, triplets
ap.rig.g2.i7: Every block opens with its own knobs, which you turn while you play; a new block shows its knobs before you add it
ap.rig.g2.i8: Vocal Rasp: a voice block that adds a blues singer's rasp, live
ap.rig.g3.i1: Each chain plays a preset from your bank, found by typing its name
ap.rig.g3.i2: Up to 8 scenes per preset (verse, chorus, solo), each with its own knob values and blocks on or off, switching with no gap
ap.rig.g3.i3: Each scene sends PC, CC, note or SysEx to your other MIDI gear when it loads
ap.rig.g3.i4: History: the last 50 versions of each preset with what changed in each, and you bring back the whole preset or a single block
ap.rig.g3.i5: Presets are text files you can copy, compare and share
ap.rig.g3.i6: Five factory presets made of built-in blocks: clean, crunch, lead, blues and ambient
ap.rig.g4.i1: Search TONE3000 inside the app by gear and format, and install a NAM capture or an IR in one click with your own key
ap.rig.g4.i2: Update a TONE3000 plugin when a newer tone is out, or uninstall it
ap.rig.g4.i3: Plugins window: all your plugins, filtered by origin, block type and name
ap.rig.g4.i4: Plugin editor: name each capture's parameters as a list, a knob or a switch, and restore any kept version
ap.rig.g4.i5: Create a plugin from your own .nam and .wav files
ap.rig.g4.i6: Create a modeling: from A2 captures taken in a grid, JoVee trains one NAM whose knobs turn continuously
ap.rig.g4.i7: Export a plugin to a single file and import it on another computer
ap.rig.g5.i1: Drum machine: 75 grooves in 15 genres on 2 sampled kits, and a fill whenever you ask
ap.rig.g5.i2: One project tempo, nudged or tapped in the top bar: the metronome, the drums and the synced delays follow it
ap.rig.g5.i3: Metronome from 30 to 300 BPM, with time signature, subdivision, three click sounds and a count-in
ap.rig.g5.i4: Backing tracks by part (solo, rhythm, bass, acoustic), plus your own WAV, FLAC, MP3, OGG or M4A files
ap.rig.g5.i5: Play a track slower or faster with the same pitch (0.5× to 2×), in another key (±12 semitones), with an A–B loop
ap.rig.g5.i6: Each groove and each track can switch your chains to the preset and scene saved with it
ap.rig.g5.i7: Drums, metronome and tracks each play on the outputs you choose
ap.rig.g5.i8: JoVee Ruler: the harmonic field and the scale of any key
ap.rig.g5.i9: Export a groove or a track to a file and import it on another computer
ap.rig.g6.i1: Up to 8 loopers per chain; each new loop locks to the length of the first, and they all restart together
ap.rig.g6.i2: Each loop records the dry guitar and keeps the preset it was recorded with, so you solo over it with another tone
ap.rig.g6.i3: Per looper: the input it records, the outputs it plays on, level, speed ½×, 1× or 2× and reverse
ap.rig.g6.i4: Waveform editor: Fit cuts the take to whole passes of the riff, plus trim, crop, cut, undo and redo
ap.rig.g6.i5: A footswitch records, plays, stops and clears the looper of the active chain
ap.rig.g6.i6: Save a take to a library every project sees, and export it to a file
ap.rig.g6.i7: Virtual DI: a recorded dry guitar (a bundled loop, a saved take or any WAV) loops through the chain while you shape the tone with both hands free
ap.rig.g7.i1: One tuner per input: tune one guitar while another one plays
ap.rig.g7.i2: Spectrum: 63 bands for each output, left and right, in real time
ap.rig.g7.i3: Harmonics: each note's harmonics on a 24-fret neck or a keyboard, with sustain, brightness, attack and dissonance
ap.rig.g7.i4: Harmonics read after any block of the chain, with sustain and intonation for every note you played
ap.rig.g7.i5: Tone Doctor: shows which block causes fizz, mud or boom for the genre you play, and which knob to turn
ap.rig.g8.i1: Mixer: a fader, mute and solo for every input and output of your interfaces
ap.rig.g8.i2: Each chain has its own fader on each output it plays, on top of the global one
ap.rig.g8.i3: Faders for each chain's volume (up to 200%), its DI and each of its loopers
ap.rig.g8.i4: Input and output meters for each chain, named after the interface and its channels
ap.rig.g9.i1: Compact view: all of a chain's knobs on one screen, with its mixer, DI, looper, Tone Doctor and meters
ap.rig.g9.i3: MIDI Learn: press a footswitch or turn a knob and choose what it does
ap.rig.g9.i4: A standard MIDI map with 34 commands, ready profiles for known controllers, and Bluetooth MIDI
ap.rig.g9.i5: Remote control from a phone or another computer, over the network or Bluetooth, with live meters, tuner, spectrum and harmonics
ap.rig.g9.i6: MCP: an AI (Claude, Cursor) builds tones and changes the open rig by conversation
ap.rig.g10.i1: A setup wizard on first launch: language, interface, inputs and outputs, TONE3000 key, and a first chain with a riff to hear it
ap.rig.g10.i2: Named inputs and outputs, channel by channel, in mono, dual mono or stereo
ap.rig.g10.i3: Three looks: Classic, Neon and Rack
ap.rig.g10.i4: Nine languages: English, Português, Español, Français, Deutsch, 日本語, 한국어, 中文 and हिन्दी
ap.rig.g10.i5: Choose the folder for presets, plugins, takes, backing tracks and drum kits
ap.rig.g10.i6: Autosave writes every change to the project
ap.rig.g10.i7: One settings file for every JoVee app: change the interface in another app and the open Rig follows
ap.rig.g10.i8: Updates from inside the app when a new version comes out
